Tanya ran into an issue when trying to switch a UAS device from the BOT
configuration to the UAS configuration via the bConfigurationValue sysfs
file.  Before installing the UAS configuration
calls usb_disable_device().  That function is supposed to remove all host
controller resources associated with that device
in the xHCI host controller.
usb: allow drivers to use allocated bandwidth until unbound
added a call to usb_disable_device() in usb_set_configuration()
the xHCI bandwidth functions were invoked.  That commit fixed a bug
also introduced a bug that is triggered when a configured device is
switched to a new configuration.
usb_disable_device() goes through all the motions of unbinding the drivers
attached to active interfaces and removing the USB core structures
associated with those interfaces
column2: but it doesn't actually remove the

column1: endpoints from the internal xHCI host controller bandwidth structures.
When usb_disable_device() calls usb_disable_endpoint() with reset_hardware
set to true
column2: the entries in udev->ep_out and udev->ep_in will be set to

column1: NULL.  Usually
column2: when the USB core installs a new configuration

column1: usb_hcd_alloc_bandwidth() will drop all non-NULL endpoints in udev->ep_out
and udev->ep_in before adding any new endpoints.  However
UAS configuration was added
old endpoints in the BOT configuration were dropped.
The xHCI driver blindly added the UAS configuration endpoints
the endpoint addresses overlapped with the old BOT configuration
endpoints.  This caused the xHCI host to reject the Configure Endpoint
command.  Now that the xHCI driver code is cleaned up to reject a
double-add of active endpoints
column2: we need to fix the USB core to properly

column1: drop old endpoints in usb_disable_device().
If the host controller driver needs bandwidth checking support
usb_disable_device() call usb_disable_endpoint() with
reset_hardware set to false
column2: drop the endpoints from the xHCI host

column1: controller
column2: and then call usb_disable_endpoint() again with

column1: reset_hardware set to true.
The first call to usb_disable_endpoint() will cancel any pending URBs and
wait on them to be freed in usb_hcd_disable_endpoint()
pointers in udev->ep_out and udev->ep in intact.  Then
usb_hcd_alloc_bandwidth() will use those pointers to know which endpoints
to drop.
The final call to usb_disable_endpoint() will do two things:
1. It will call usb_hcd_disable_endpoint() again
since the ep->urb_list should be empty after the first call to
usb_disable_endpoint() returns.
2. It will set the entries in udev->ep_out and udev->ep in to NULL
usb_hcd_disable_endpoint().  That call will have no effect
driver doesn't set the endpoint_disable function pointer.
Note that usb_disable_device() will now need to be called with
hcd->bandwidth_mutex held.
This should be backported to kernels as old as 2.6.32.
